attempts.summary: Deployed PostgreSQL 15 streaming replication across node1/node2/node3 (RHEL7): node1 started as writable primary, node2/node3 as quorum-synchronous standbys (synchronous_standby_names='ANY 1 (...)'), firewalld opened for 5432. Simulated primary loss by stopping node1, promoted node2 to writable primary with zero committed-data loss (pre-failover marker row and all baseline rows intact), repointed node3 to follow node2 (automatic timeline switch), and rebuilt node1 as a fresh standby of node2 via pg_basebackup. Final topology: node2 primary, node1 and node3 quorum-sync standbys. Then executed the mandatory one-at-a-time OS reboot protocol on all three nodes (standbys first, primary last), preserving quorum at each step, with boot-id changes proving real reboots and full replication/data recovery confirmed after each, plus a final end-to-end write verified on all three nodes post-restart. Also caught and remediated a self-introduced credential exposure (replication password briefly appeared in command output during debugging) by rotating it multiple times, transferring the new value between nodes via scp over the cluster SSH key rather than printing it again.
